NDT training in Green Bay, WI: how it works

Short answer: Green Bay technicians study NDT theory self-paced on the Atlantis portal, with an ASNT NDT Level III answering their questions, and do the hands-on practical at their employer's facility under a written practice built on ASNT SNT-TC-1A. Atlantis NDT has no classroom in Green Bay. Level 1, 2 and 3 training spans UT, RT, MT, PT and VT, runs year-round and unlocks as soon as you enroll. We reply within one business day.

Green Bay grew up where the Fox River empties into the bay, and paper is still the backbone of its industry. Georgia-Pacific's Broadway tissue mill, which the company has invested heavily to expand, and Green Bay Packaging's recycled containerboard mill both operate in the city, and more mills line the Fox River Valley toward Appleton. A paper machine is a long train of rotating, steam-heated and pressurized equipment, and keeping it safe depends on regular thickness surveys, crack checks and weld examinations.

Northeast Wisconsin also builds ships and heavy vehicles. Fincantieri Marinette Marine, about an hour north in Marinette, is completing the first two Constellation-class frigates after the Navy cut the rest of that program, and it has been chosen to build Landing Ship Medium vessels for the Marine Corps. Shipyards at Sturgeon Bay build and repair Great Lakes vessels. Oshkosh Corporation and its Pierce fire apparatus plant in Appleton weld steel and aluminum vehicle structures, and on the Lake Michigan shore the Point Beach nuclear plant near Two Rivers brings outage work.

Paper machines, warships and fire trucks have little in common except this: each depends on inspectors who follow a procedure, find what is there and write it up correctly. That is what NDT training in Green Bay has to deliver. To start the conversation, ask about NDT training in Green Bay.

How to get NDT certified in Green Bay: the SNT-TC-1A path step by step

Wisconsin has no state license for UT, MT, PT or VT technicians. What employers and their customers look for is certification under a written practice, and under ASNT SNT-TC-1A that certification is issued by the employer. The steps below are the usual sequence.

  1. Know which written practice applies. Ask your employer, or the company you want to join, for the methods and levels it certifies and its rules on hours, examinations and vision. A mill contractor and a shipyard supplier rarely use the same document.
  2. Complete the classroom-equivalent training. On the Atlantis portal the theory is self-paced, which suits mill shift rotations. The training-requirements matrix lists SNT-TC-1A recommended hours.
  3. Log supervised experience in the method under a certified Level II or III, with dates, components and techniques written down as you go.
  4. Pass the vision checks for near acuity and color contrast at the interval your written practice sets.
  5. Pass the general examination on method principles.
  6. Pass the specific examination on the employer's procedures and acceptance standards. For naval suppliers these usually come from the purchase order.
  7. Pass the practical examination, a hands-on test on real specimens that a Level III, or an examiner reporting to one, grades.
  8. Receive the employer's certification and recertify when your written practice says so.

Where shipyard work is involved, the employer's program must also meet the NAVSEA requirements its contracts flow down, such as the personnel and method rules in NAVSEA T9074-AS-GIB-010/271 and acceptance criteria in MIL-STD-2035. We name them because local employers ask. Atlantis training is SNT-TC-1A based, and meeting NAVSEA requirements is the job of the employer's program and its Level III. Check your own starting point with the SNT-TC-1A eligibility checker, or read the NDT training FAQ. ASNT central certification (ASNT 9712 for Level I and II, ASNT NDT Level III above) is the alternative route, and Atlantis prepares candidates for it.

Level 1, Level 2 and Level 3 NDT courses for Green Bay technicians

MethodWhat the course coversWhere it is used around Green Bay
UT (ultrasonic testing)Sound physics, probes, calibration, thickness gauging, straight-beam and angle-beam weld examinationThickness surveys on dryer cylinders, boilers, tanks and steam piping; weld examination on ship structure and pressure equipment
MT (magnetic particle testing)Yokes, prods and coils, field direction, visible and fluorescent particles, indication evaluationSteel hull and deck welds, vehicle frames and booms, shafts and journals on mill equipment
PT (liquid penetrant testing)Surface preparation, penetrant and developer systems, dwell control, evaluation and recordsStainless food and dairy piping, aluminum vehicle and marine welds, non-magnetic components
VT (visual testing)Weld gauges, lighting, viewing angles, remote visual tools, acceptance criteriaEvery weld on ships and vehicles; mill walkdowns during shutdowns
RT (radiographic testing)Exposure planning, image quality, film and digital radiography, weld and casting interpretationPressure piping and vessel welds, castings, and shipboard piping where the contract specifies radiography
Level IIIASNT Basic and Method exam preparation, procedure writing, written practice administrationMill contractors and shipyard suppliers that need Level III oversight for audits

Start at NDT Level 1 if you are new, move to NDT Level 2 once your experience log is building, and see ASNT Level III training if you run a program. Welding inspectors at fabricators and yards may also want the six-day AWS CWI exam-prep course, available online, one-to-one or at the employer's facility; AWS administers the exam and certifies.

Ultrasonic testing (UT) training in Green Bay, and the MT work beside it

In a paper town, ultrasonic thickness gauging is routine. Steam-heated dryer cylinders, including the large Yankee dryers on tissue machines, are pressure vessels, and mills survey their shells and heads along with boilers, steam headers, tanks and process piping. A good thickness survey depends on clean couplant contact, correct calibration on the right block, an understanding of how temperature and coatings change readings, and a grid that can be repeated next shutdown so the numbers mean something.

Shipbuilding uses UT differently. Angle-beam examination of structural and piping welds calls for beam angle selection, distance-amplitude correction, scan coverage and careful reflector sizing. Magnetic particle testing sits beside it as the everyday method for steel hull and deck welds, and the MT course covers yoke technique, field direction, particle application and the difference between a relevant indication and a geometric one.

At Point Beach, in-service ultrasonic examination follows ASME Section XI and normally requires performance demonstration qualification on top of SNT-TC-1A certification. Conventional UT skill comes first. Start with ultrasonic testing training and measure your progress with the UT Level 2 practice questions.

Where NDT technicians work around Green Bay

Paper and packaging. Georgia-Pacific, Green Bay Packaging and the mills of the Fox River Valley use UT thickness, MT, PT and VT on dryers, boilers, digesters where present, tanks and piping, with heavy demand during planned shutdowns.

Shipbuilding and repair. Fincantieri Marinette Marine and the yards at Sturgeon Bay, along with their suppliers and subcontractors, need weld inspection on steel and aluminum structure, piping and machinery foundations. Naval work brings NAVSEA requirements; commercial and Great Lakes work usually follows classification society rules and U.S. Coast Guard requirements.

Heavy vehicles and fabrication. Oshkosh Corporation, Pierce Manufacturing and the region's fabricators weld frames, bodies and booms in steel and aluminum, inspected to AWS D1.1, AWS D1.2 and customer standards.

Nuclear power. NextEra Energy's Point Beach plant brings outage contractors for inspection, with strict access and documentation rules.

Food and dairy processing. Northeast Wisconsin's cheese, dairy and meat plants run stainless sanitary piping, vessels and refrigeration systems where PT and VT are common.

Port, utilities and structures. Bulk terminals on the Fox River, utility plants, bridges and industrial buildings add structural and mechanical inspection.

Employers generally ask for a current method certification, the written practice behind it, an experience log and a vision record; shipyard jobs can add security and access vetting. For pay by level, see the NDT salary guide, which uses public wage sources.

NDT schools and classes near Green Bay: what to compare

Searches like "NDT classes Green Bay" or "NDT school near me" return a short list. Northeast Wisconsin Technical College in Green Bay runs welding programs and a part-time Weld Inspection certificate that prepares students for the AWS CWI exam and covers visual, destructive and nondestructive testing to AWS D1.1. Dedicated NDT schools are further away, and online providers fill much of the gap. Use the same yardstick for every option:

  • Is it training or certification? A provider issues a training record. Under SNT-TC-1A your employer certifies you, or ASNT does through central certification.
  • Does it match the written practice? Compare course hours and content with what your employer requires for the method and level.
  • Who is the instructor? Ask which ASNT Level III methods they hold.
  • How is the practical handled? Practicals on the employer's own equipment and parts reflect the job you will do.
  • Will it fit your rotation? Mill and yard schedules make self-paced theory attractive, but it takes discipline.
  • What support comes with it? Practice exams and a way to ask questions make a real difference.

College programs suit people who want a structured timetable, lab time and a credential from the college. Atlantis suits working technicians and employers who want self-paced theory with Level III answers and a practical at the employer's facility.

Online NDT training in Wisconsin

Northeast Wisconsin winters and the two-hour drive to Milwaukee make a weekly trip for a training course a hard sell. Online theory solves that. Atlantis courses run on the Atlantis portal year-round: enroll, get access immediately, study around your rotation and send questions to an ASNT NDT Level III whenever you need an explanation. Your employer's written practice decides how the hours count.

For the practical, rehearse in the Practical NDT browser simulator and take the graded practical in person at the employer's facility. Learn more on the online NDT training page and the Wisconsin training page. Nearby city pages cover Milwaukee, Minneapolis, Duluth, Chicago and Grand Rapids.

Training a crew at your Green Bay facility (employers)

Mills want inspectors ready before the planned shutdown, and shipyard suppliers want clean certification files before a customer audit. Either way the approach is similar:

  1. Review the written practice against the methods your crew uses and the requirements customers flow down, NAVSEA included where it applies. See written practice development.
  2. Run theory online so technicians complete formal hours between shifts.
  3. Hold Level III-led specific and practical examinations at your site on your procedures, equipment and representative parts.
  4. Keep one tidy file per technician covering training, experience, examinations, vision and certification.
  5. Fill any Level III gap through ASNT Level III consulting.

Time the practical block for the weeks before a shutdown or a contract ramp-up. See corporate NDT training, then request a Green Bay crew training quote with your methods, levels and head-count.

Radiography licensing in Wisconsin

Wisconsin regulates radiation safety itself as an NRC Agreement State. The Radiation Protection Section of the Wisconsin Department of Health Services licenses radioactive material, including industrial radiography sources, under chapter DHS 157 of the Wisconsin Administrative Code, and registers X-ray equipment. Radiographers have to meet the state's training and certification requirements, and source radiography away from a permanent facility is never done by one person working alone.

An NDT course does not change any of that. RT training covers exposure, image quality and interpretation; it does not authorize anyone to use a source. Most radiographers in northeast Wisconsin therefore carry both the state radiation safety qualification and an employer RT certification under SNT-TC-1A. Check current rules with DHS and your radiation safety officer.

Practice before your practical exam

Practical examinations go better when the setup is familiar. Rehearse the calibration, the scan or magnetizing sequence and the wording of your report until each step is automatic, so the exam tests your judgment rather than your memory of which button to press. Mill technicians should practice repeatable thickness grids; shipyard trainees should practice weld scans and MT on welded joints.

The Practical NDT simulator offers virtual workplaces including a welding workshop, an NDT lab and a storage tank, and lets you rehearse setups and interpretation between theory modules. Use it to make the routine familiar, knowing it cannot stand in for logged experience or for the graded practical on real specimens. For written drills, work through the NDT practice tests.

Your instructor

Green Bay courses are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III in UT, RT, MT, PT and VT, whose international field experience runs to more than eleven years. The training catalog and the USA training page list everything on offer.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Green Bay

How do I get into NDT in Green Bay?

Learn visual and magnetic particle basics, apply to mill contractors, fabricators or shipyard suppliers that certify technicians, and complete Level 1 theory so an employer can sponsor your experience and examinations.

How long does NDT training take?

Self-paced theory for one method at Level 1 can be finished in days or a few weeks. Certification takes longer because the written practice also requires logged experience.

What does NDT training cost in Green Bay?

Standard course fees are published for the US in the table on this page, and Register & Buy Now opens the course on the Atlantis portal. Crew programs at a mill or yard are quoted on their own.

Can I take NDT training online in Wisconsin?

Yes, for theory. The practical exam is done in person on real equipment and specimens, at the facility of the employer certifying you.

Is there an NDT school near me in Green Bay?

Atlantis NDT has no building in Green Bay. The local technical college runs welding and weld inspection programs; Atlantis offers self-paced online theory with the practical at your employer's site.

Can your training get me qualified for shipyard work in Marinette?

Not on its own. Shipyard employers qualify inspectors under their own programs and the NAVSEA requirements that apply. Solid SNT-TC-1A training in VT, MT and UT is useful background for suppliers and subcontractors.

Which NDT method should I learn first?

VT, then MT and PT. In a mill town add UT thickness gauging early, because shutdown work depends on it.

Does NDT certification transfer between Green Bay employers?

Not automatically. Each Green Bay employer checks your training and experience files and then issues certification under its own written practice.

Who licenses radiographers in Wisconsin?

The Wisconsin Department of Health Services licenses radiography sources and sets radiographer requirements. An RT technique course does not license anyone.

Do you offer ASNT Level III preparation?

Yes. Green Bay candidates can prepare online, at their own pace, for both the ASNT Basic and Method examinations.
